source_text:
Στίχ. β΄. καὶ ἰδὼν Βαλάκ. Ἤκουσαν ἔθνη καὶ ὠργίσθησαν. Ἐν οἷς καὶ τό· Ἄρχοντες Μωαβιτῶν, ἔλαβεν αὐτοὺς τρόμος.
Στίχ. δ΄. (23) Ὅτι ὥσπερ μάντιν τὸν μισθὸν ταύτης ἔφερον προσαγαγεῖν αὐτόν.
thought_title: Balak's seeing and the nations' fear
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 22:2, where Balak sees what Israel has done, and he connects this with a scriptural passage about nations hearing and being angry, with Moabite rulers seized by trembling.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 2. And Balak having seen. [The] nations heard and were angered. Among which also this: Rulers of [the] Moabites, trembling seized them. Verse 4. (23) That just as [a] seer the wage of this [woman] they were bringing to bring him forward.

choices.why: The participle is aorist active, and the name is nominative; the literal rendering preserves the participial construction rather than turning it into a finite clause.
The aorist passive of ὀργίζω means to become angry; 'were angered' keeps the passive morphology visible, unlike 'grew angry' which hides it.
The verb λαμβάνω with τρόμος as subject is a common idiom for being seized by fear; the word order subject-verb-object is preserved.
The glossary does not cover this term, but μάντις means a diviner or seer; 'seer' is the standard rendering and fits the context of Balaam being summoned.
The demonstrative pronoun is feminine genitive singular, referring to a woman previously mentioned; the literal rendering preserves the gender and case.

pass_b_english: Verse 2. And Balak having seen. Nations heard and were angered. Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and trembling seized them.
Verse 4. (23) Because they were bringing his fee as for a seer, to bring him forward.

problems.source_quote: Ἐν οἷς καὶ ... Ἄρχοντες Μωαβιτῶν, ἔλαβεν αὐτοὺς τρόμος
problems.why: The source says “among them also” (referring to the Moabite rulers), not “among these words”. Adding “words” misrepresents the clause.
problems.fix: Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and fear seized them.
problems.ruling: Ἐν οἷς means 'among whom/them,' referring to the Moabites, not 'among these words.' Adding 'words' misrepresents the reference.

edits.old: Among these words is also: Rulers of the Moabites, trembling seized them.
edits.new: Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and trembling seized them.

fixed: The source 'Ἐν οἷς καὶ τό· Ἄρχοντες Μωαβιτῶν, ἔλαβεν αὐτοὺς τρόμος' refers to the Moabite rulers among those who heard and were angered, not to words; the English added 'words', so I corrected it to 'Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and trembling seized them.'

last_rejected.quote: Among them also were the Moabite rulers, and trembling seized them.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐν οἷς καὶ τό· Ἄρχοντες Μωαβιτῶν, ἔλαβεν αὐτοὺς τρόμος.
last_rejected.why: Ἐν οἷς means 'in which [words/passages]', not 'among them [the nations]'. Origen refers to a scriptural passage, not people.
last_rejected.fix: In which passage also is: 'The rulers of Moab, trembling seized them.'
last_rejected.ruling: Ἐν οἷς is dative plural ‘among which/among them’, fitting the context of nations, so ‘among them also were the Moabite rulers’ is appropriate.
